target_material: Nickel compounds (e.g., NiO, NiNx, NiCx, NiSix, NiSx)
summary: The study investigates the surface thermolytic behavior of Ni(amd)2, a nickel amidinate precursor, and its implications for ALD of nickel compounds. The Ni(amd)2 precursor reacts with SiOx surfaces at room temperature, forming Ni−O bonds and byproduct Hamd. The decomposition of the amidinate moiety occurs at 250 °C, leading to carbon and nitrogen impurities. The study demonstrates that ALD of NiO can be achieved at low temperatures (90 °C) but higher temperatures (e.g., 150–200 °C) reduce impurities. The results highlight the importance of surface thermolysis for optimizing ALD processes.
evidence: The Ni(amd)2 precursor was shown to be reactive with the SiOx surface even at room temperature, which suggests a good suitability for low-temperature ALD. The surface amidinate moiety is found to decompose at 250 °C, which suggests the limitation of Ni(amd)2 for high-temperature ALD. The NiO films can be successfully deposited at an ever-low temperature of 90 °C, and raising the deposition temperature to 200 °C can eliminate the accumulation of carbon and nitrogen impurities at the film-substrate interface.
